subject: red pandas
one_liner: The browser IDE for red panda engineers. Nine-key paw input, deploys that wait for you to wake up, and compute billed in bamboo.
brand_voice_notes: Deadpan cloud-dev-tools confidence. Every biological fact about red pandas (seventeen-hour sleep, nine-key paws, solitude, bamboo) is treated as an infrastructure constraint that has been productized. Never wink. Prices are confident, metrics are fake and precise. The company believes the tree is a deployment region.

hero.h1: Ship from the branch you never left.
hero.sub: Canopy is a cloud development environment built for red panda engineers: nine-key paw input, deploys that hold until you wake up, and compute metered in bamboo. It runs in the browser because you live in a tree.

features.title: Paw Mode
features.blurb: Your paw presses nine keys at once. The editor accepts the chord, resolves it to the statement you probably meant, and commits it. Precision typing is a primate concept we chose not to inherit.

features.title: Sleep-Safe Deploys
features.blurb: You sleep up to seventeen hours a day. Deploys queue while you are unconscious and ship the moment you stir, without review. So far this has gone fine.

features.title: Bamboo Compute
features.blurb: Compute is metered in stalks. One stalk equals one vCPU-hour. Finance asked why. The metric stays.

demo_screen_concept: The Canopy workspace itself: a browser IDE with a 'canopy view' file tree (bamboo_intake.py, nap_scheduler.js, den.config), a code editor where any keypress inserts a nine-character paw chord that resolves into clean code after a beat (Paw Mode toggle), a Run button that executes nap_scheduler.js in a fake console, a Sleep-Safe deploy panel showing 'deploys held: operator asleep' with a wake/sleep toggle that releases the queue, and a bamboo compute meter that spends stalks every time you run something.

design_direction.style: Claymorphic daylight dev-console, bamboo-leaf light mode. The page is staged as the product site of a heavily funded developer-tools company that has decided the red panda is an engineering demographic and files sleeping seventeen hours a day under continuous deployment. A pale bamboo-leaf ground (#F1F4EC) runs the whole page with no gradients, no texture washes, and no print chrome; structure comes from soft clay volume: panels are extruded slabs with 24px radii, a warm dual shadow (one soft drop below-right, one faint inner top highlight) so every card reads as something molded, cooled, and left on a shelf a red panda could bat off. The core motif is the clay keycap: a chunky extruded pill, wider than it is tall, that carries every stat, badge, tier price, and chord readout, and depresses 2px with its shadow collapsing when pressed, because the entire product is designed around a paw hitting nine of them at once. The second motif is the nap dot: a small status indicator that is asleep by default (a drowsy half-closed crescent) and only opens during live telemetry, used in the deploy queue, the header status, and the pricing SLA line. One red-panda rust (#BE5A28) carries the wordmark, every primary CTA, the highlighted word per headline, and the pressed state of active keycaps; one rationed bamboo moss (#6F8F4F) is reserved strictly for live telemetry (passing builds, released deploys, the awake state of the nap dot, stalk balances) and appears nowhere else. Bricolage Grotesque sets the wordmark and headlines in warm chunky grotesque with dev-tools-that-raised-a-B confidence; Red Hat Text carries plain, faintly changelog body copy. Every figure that pretends to be workspace telemetry (chord widths, queue depths, stalk balances, nap durations, tier prices) is set in Red Hat Mono with tabular figures inside soft inset clay wells, recessed where the keycaps are extruded, so it reads like the meter, not marketing. Motion is clay-restrained: keycaps and cards squish to scale 1.02 on hover with the drop shadow deepening, CTAs depress 2px on press with the shadow collapsing, the nap dot blinks awake once when telemetry updates then droops again on a 6s cycle, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur panels, no hairline print rules, no hard offset ink shadows, no bento lattice, no didone engraving, no HUD brackets, no nautical chrome, no storefront capsules, no engraved seals, no emoji. Reads like a company that files hibernation under 'asynchronous workflows' and considers the thumb a legacy peripheral.

fonts.body: 'Red Hat Text', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: developer-tools product page: hero with claim plus a CSS-built clay IDE window, feature trio on clay slabs, deadpan testimonials, three-tier pricing on keycaps, single footer CTA
design_direction.motion_vocab: clay squish on hover (scale 1.02, shadow deepens), 2px depress on press with shadow collapse, nap dot blinks awake then droops on a 6s cycle, sections fade up 6px with 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero: left column carries the h1 with 'branch' in red-panda rust and the primary CTA as an oversized clay keycap; right column is a CSS-molded IDE window (clay slab with inset editor well, file-tree leaves, a mono deploy ticker reading DEPLOYS HELD: OPERATOR ASLEEP). If the step-4 hero image lands, it sits behind the IDE slab as a rounded clay-framed portrait; if not, the IDE slab stands alone.
